revision_key.description: The design revision key: lowercase hex SHA-256 of the a1 preimage (revision-key.md, "Hashing"). Never truncated.

object_format.description: Object format of the repository; hashed into the key.

source.description: Commit or working tree. Not hashed.

config.description: The effective configuration that was hashed, after validation; the default one when `--config` was not given.

config_digest.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical config bytes; the commit index's config column.

entries.description: The source set, sorted by `path` in code point order (UTF-8 byte order); the order they are hashed in. Always holds the project file.

warnings.description: Non-fatal findings (for example `lfs-filter-unavailable`), sorted by `code`, then `message`, in code point order. Empty when there are none.

description:
Output of `prism-kicad revision-key`: the key with everything needed to
recompute and audit it. Printed on stdout as one compact JSON document
followed by LF (conventions.md §13).
title: Revision key record a1

Sha256Hex.description: Lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest: exactly 64 characters, no prefix such as `sha256:`.

RevisionKeyObjectFormat.description: Object format of the repository, as `git rev-parse --show-object-format` prints it.

RevisionKeySource.description: Where the listing came from. The same content gives the same key either way.

path.description: Repository-relative path, exactly the bytes git lists (UTF-8, never Unicode-normalized or case-folded).

kind.description: Entry kind, from the git mode and object type.

object_id.description: Blob id (regular, executable, symlink) or recorded commit id (gitlink), in the repository's object format.

category.description: Selection rule the entry matched; not hashed.

RevisionKeyEntry.description: One entry of the source set: a tree entry the key hashes.

total.description: All selected entries: the sum of the fields above, equal to the length of `entries`.

RevisionKeyCounts.description: Number of selected entries per category. Each field is the count of entries whose `category` is the matching value.

code.description: Stable code that tools and tests match on.

message.description: One-sentence explanation for people; its wording may change between versions.

Warning.description:
A finding with a stable code and a human-readable message. Whether it is a
warning or an error is given by the array that holds it. Field names are
the same in snake_case and camelCase documents.

commit.description: The full commit id the given revision resolved to (`git rev-parse --verify <rev>^{commit}`).

RevisionKeyCommitSource.description: The key was computed from a commit's tree (`--commit`).

RevisionKeyWorktreeSource.description: The key was computed from the working tree (`--worktree`): the tree `git add -A` would stage, computed without writing.

RepoPath.description:
Repository-relative POSIX path, exactly as `git ls-tree` names the entry:
`/`-separated, case preserved, no leading `/`, no empty, `.` or `..`
segment, no backslash and no `:`. The same character rule as ArchivePath.
It is the only path type in bundle documents: a file has one spelling
whichever project in the repository refers to it, and a file outside the
project directory needs no `..`.

RevisionKeyEntryKind.description:
Kind of a source-set entry, fixed by its git tree mode and object type. The
hashed framing spells each kind as git does (revision-key.md, "Hashing").

GitObjectId.description:
Git object id in lowercase hexadecimal: 40 characters in a SHA-1
repository, 64 in a SHA-256 repository. Used for commit ids and blob ids.

RevisionKeySourceCategory.description:
Why an entry is in the source set, from its file name (revision-key.md,
"Selection"). Name rules are ASCII case-insensitive. Not hashed: it is
derived from the path and kind.

Count.description: A count of things: a non-negative safe integer.

DiagnosticCode.description:
Stable machine-readable code of a finding, in lowercase kebab-case, for
example `stale-saved-fills` or `net-mismatch`. A code never changes meaning
once published; a new meaning gets a new code.
